insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Ad tech sells inferred intent at $5–$150 CPA; this protocol settles a cryptographically signed purchase confirmation at roughly $0.10 per event — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't a pricing advantage, it's a different category of data entirely.

insights.topic: Cookie deprecation creates structural gap this fills
insights.insight: With Chrome joining Safari and Firefox in eliminating cross-site cookies, the industry's primary attribution primitive is gone — and the replacements (fingerprinting, data brokers, first-party data) are all probabilistic and narrowing under GDPR/CCPA pressure; verified receipt data sidesteps this entirely because the purchase event is the proof, not a modeled proxy for it.

insights.topic: Physical commerce dominates the signal set
insights.insight: Grocery, dining, and gas together account for 56% of verified receipts in the trailing 14-day window — high-frequency categories where brand marketers have historically had the weakest closed-loop attribution because transactions happen off-platform and out of sight.

The unresolved 'Unknown' category carries a $107 average basket — roughly 2–2.5x the classified categories — suggesting the store resolver is missing a disproportionate share of high-value purchases; brands in big-ticket retail should treat this as an early data-quality flag before building targeting models on it.

insights.topic: Growth rate compounding despite suppressed volume
insights.insight: Velocity sits below 1.0x week-over-week but acceleration has held above 1.0x for six or more consecutive cycles, meaning the rate of growth is itself growing even while raw throughput is muted — a pattern that typically precedes a volume inflection rather than a plateau.

insights.topic: Geographic expansion follows social graph, not paid acquisition
insights.insight: New metro clusters appeared in sustained bursts of 7–9 CBSAs per cycle across five consecutive heartbeats before this consolidation cycle — a diffusion pattern consistent with peer-to-peer adoption, which implies the user base has genuine behavioral cohesion rather than paid-install demographics that erode quickly.
